articles.title: ‘They’re Still Humans Like the Rest of Us’: Watch the ‘Everest: The Other Side’ Directors Discuss Relating to Extreme Athletes
articles.summary: At IndieWire's Art of the Doc event, Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin explained what draws them to some of the world's biggest risk-takers.
articles.content: Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin know a thing or two about extreme athletes. From the daring rock climbing of “Free Solo” to their new film “Everest: The Other Side,” which follows Jim Morrison’s attempts to fulfill his late wife Hilaree Nelson’s dream of skiing down the world’s tallest mountain, the documentarians love to capture fearless people drawn to extreme challenges. During a conversation about “Everest” with IndieWire features writer Alison Foreman at our Art of the Doc event in Los Angeles, the filmmakers discussed what draws them to the subject matter over and over again. “In all our films, you think you’re seeing these exceptional, extraordinary, extreme athletes. But at the end of the day they’re still human beings like the rest of us,” Chin said. “What I’m interested in bridging that gap where people feel like they can’t relate to people out there doing these things. But the story is really human, and this film is about very human experiences. Even though they’re climbing and skiiing the most extreme places in the world.” Related Stories Yes, That’s a Wicker Penis: Inside Alexander Skarsgård’s Wild ‘Wicker’ Transformation ‘Marie Antoinette’ at 20: Sofia Coppola on How the Film Almost Broke Her, the Critical Backlash, and Paying Tribute to Mom Vasarhelyi also emphasized the fact that each documentary subject is a different person with their own unique story to tell. In the case of Nelson, she saw someone who was deeply goal-oriented but lacked the grand romanticizations about her sport that drive so many other athletes. She saw the adventurer as a fellow parent who lived a fairly normal life when she wasn’t pushing herself to scale the world’s highest peaks. “I had met a lot of extreme athletes, but Hilaree had a candor to her vocation that I hadn’t heard before,” Vasarhelyi said. “It’s not romantic. articles.content: As all linear TV brands grapple with audiences migrating to YouTube, the Murdoch-run cable news empire has yet to have a crisis of confidence. For 30 years it has been ruthless about focusing on what its viewers want. On Oct. 6, Fox News Media CEO Suzanne Scott gathered with her senior leadership team and some Fox News originals like Steve Doocy, Brit Hume and Trace Gallagher in Nasdaq’s Studio A, right in the middle of Times Square, to ring the closing bell. A few minutes before she rang the bell, Scott took to the podium to deliver remarks celebrating Fox News Channel’s 30th anniversary, recognizing a media platform that transformed not only the cable news landscape, but the political landscape as well. “As we celebrate 30 years of stories reported and analyzed, and history witnessed at each turn, we also look ahead because the next chapter of media is being shaped right now by new technology, new platforms, and new ways of connecting with audiences,” the CEO added. Fox News is a powerful force in American politics and culture, and a dominant one at that. It decimates the cable news competition in the ratings (it now tops CNN and MS NOW combined handily), and over the last year has had its sights set on the broadcast networks. And an interview on the channel can still make or break powerful figures. Just look at Katie Zacharia. The newly-minted White House press secretary was facing a barrage of criticism over her first press conference earlier this month, and questions over whether she was really a working lawyer. But it was a Sean Hannity interview that was the final straw, with the Fox News host interrogating her about the criticisms and her past statements. The next morning, the White House said that she would be exiting the role after only five days on the job, with some pundits comparing her appearance on Hannity to a mob hit. articles.content: An exclusive excerpt from Jonathan Van Meter’s ‘Citizen Kim’ reveals how a French Impressionist masterpiece ended up on her bathroom wall. One day in early February 2022, I was hanging out at Kim’s office as she tried to cram two cover shoots into one day. Between the shoots, Kim was back in her glam room, getting RE-glammed with different hair and new makeup, this time to shoot the cover of Vogue Hong Kong. Kim was effusive and bossy, running her multibillion-dollar business in a bathrobe, two gay men pulling at her hair and face. At one point, as she was helped into and then out of a complicated, totally sheer Schiaparelli tulle dress — it was pretty much nothing but scaffolding — I looked up from my phone and she was entirely naked. Neither of us flinched. Lately, she and I had been playing a little game of “Guess What Happened in 1995?” because we kept being surprised by the astonishing number of cultural and technological shifts — to say nothing of her own complicated personal circumstances — that unfolded in that one year. Once she was dressed and sitting back in her chair, I said to Kim, “You know what else happened in 1995?” She looked at me expectantly. The movie Clueless came out (her favorite film). When it was first released, Kim and her father (and a group of Kim’s friends and their fathers) all went to see it together. “We were dying at every reference,” she told me. “It was so me in high school. … I had pretty much every outfit that the girls wore in Clueless . … I was still into Contempo Casuals and shopping at Judy’s at the Century City Mall. … Like, when I saw that movie, I couldn’t believe it. articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: The process to find out the next James Bond has been long and thorough, but all signs are pointing to the search hitting the homestretch as Amazon MGM Studios is setting its final auditions over the next week. Sources tell Deadline that screen tests for the Bond role could begin as early as Friday and go through the next week for its final group. Watch on Deadline The process to find the next 007 goes back to the spring, when the studio announced casting director Nina Gold was joining the project and that the search was underway. Following two months of meetings, Deadline reported the first round of auditions would take place in August; since then, the studio, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve cut the list to its final group and worked out test offers in September. Since landing full creative control of the franchise last year, Amazon MGM has been thorough in its search for the behind-the-scenes talent that will be overseeing the development of this next pic in the series. Pascal and Heyman were the first to be brought on, and after meeting with a number of directors the studio tapped Villeneuve to direct. The same steps were also taken before tapping Steven Knight last summer to pen the script , and, since then, the focus has been on getting the story in the right place before auditioning actors to play the role. articles.title: How Olivia Colman Starrer ‘Wicker’ Went From Unpublished Short Story To A Big-Screen Feminist Romantasy
articles.content: When Justin Lothrop first came across Ursula Wills’ short story “The Wicker Husband” online in 2021, the Votiv Films producer immediately knew that it was material worth championing. The offbeat fantasy fable, which at its core explores themes of jealousy and the transformative power of love, was just the kind of unique IP that the Seattle and L.A.-based banner looks to back. “It hadn’t been published anywhere,” Lothrop recalls of Wills’ story, which is the source material for Olivia Colman starrer Wicker that releases in the U.S. tomorrow (October 23) via Black Bear. “She was just writing them and putting them up on a website somewhere.” For Votiv founder Brent Stiefel and Lothrop, who have built the company’s business around finding distinctive material and championing stories that might otherwise struggle to reach the screen – think Sydney Sweeney boxing title Christy and Rose Byrne comedy-drama Tow –, the premise was an immediate draw. Lothrop quickly optioned the story and sent it to producer Brad Zimmerman of Yoki, Inc., the production company founded with filmmaker David Michôd. Watch on Deadline Votiv and Yoki would ultimately enlist Save Yourselves! filmmakers Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson to write and direct the project that would later attach Colman and her South Of The River Pictures banner to embrace a film that is anything but conventional. Wicker is an audacious comedic fable about sex, marriage and the absurdities of social convention. It tells the wholly original love story of an ostracized fisherwoman, played by Colman, who commissions a husband to be made by the local basketmaker, played by Peter Dinklage. When her wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård) proves more spectacular than she ever imagined, his soulful spirit and unique prowess awaken something inside of her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of village life. articles.title: ‘Clayface’ Director James Watkins Explains Aaron Paul’s Cameo: “A Real Brief Easter Egg”
articles.content: In DC Studios ‘ Clayface , Tom Rhys Harries’ titular shape-shifting Batman villain takes multiple forms, including a surprising familiar face. Following murmurs of a cameo, director James Watkins confirmed that Aaron Paul makes a brief appearance in the DCU movie as Matt’s (Harries) father, who raised him in the slums of Gotham City. “He has a real brief Easter egg kind of moment,” Watkins told Entertainment Weekly . While flashbacks of Paul as Matt’s father were ultimately cut from the film, the Breaking Bad alum makes a quick appearance in the action-packed Club Vesuvius scene, in which Matt shape-shifts into multiple people to take on Szabo’s (David Dencik) goons before taking has dad’s form to kill Jimmy “One Nut” (Enzo Squillino Jr.), the gangster who took his father’s life years before. Watch on Deadline “In terms of trying to figure out the character, it was, How much is Matt defined by his past and how much is he an everyman?” the director explained. “At one point, we were looking at it and thinking, Is it the ‘sins of the father’?” Watkins continued, “But actually, as we worked on the script, I thought that notion of revenge was more universal and more relatable to all of us. It doesn’t matter whether you’re carrying a trauma or any of that. If we’re slighted, we carry this sense of being wronged and we all want to do something, but generally in life we can’t do anything about it and we’re powerless.” Now playing in theaters, Clayface stars Harries as rising actor Matt Hagen, who suffers gruesome wounds after the brutal mafioso Szabo (Dencik) cuts up his face, resulting in the downfall of his career. But when he discovers the groundbreaking nanotech research of Dr. Caitlyn Corr (Naomi Ackie), Matt convinces her to restore his face to its former glory, only to result in terrifying side effects and a bloody quest for revenge.

articles.title: Inside The BBC Cuts: Painful Service Closures Begin, But Worse Could Be To Come
articles.content: “The world needs the BBC more than ever. It might be a different size and shape. It’s not going to be a so-so Netflix or a me-too YouTube. It’s going to be a better BBC.” That was the message Matt Brittin left ringing in the ears of BBC staff when concluding a town hall last month. The director general was attempting to lift the gloom after being beset with questions from anxious employees about job losses, service reductions, and general retrenchment. He has an uneviable task. Brittin is grappling with a financial crisis that is precipitating some of the most painful cuts in the BBC’s history. He is also attempting to cement the BBC’s position as Britain’s premium media brand in an era of unprecedented competition. The BBC must save £500 million ($670M) by 2028 after hemorrhaging more than two million licence fee payers since 2020. Despite relentless internal memos about layoffs and content cuts since the summer, the BBC has only announced £200M of its half-billion goal. In other words, it’s not even halfway through the cuts. articles.title: Kore-eda Hirokazu Explains Why He Never Films Children Crying – and What Ken Loach and Hou Hsiao-hsien Taught Him
articles.content: Japanese auteur Kore-eda Hirokazu , whose films are known for their natural performances from child actors, said there is one thing he has decided never to put on screen: a child crying. “It’s not that I can’t, or that it’s difficult. I don’t shoot it,” the Japanese director said at an In Conversation event at the the Singapore International Film Festival on Saturday. “The ideal is that after viewers finish watching, they remember that child’s smile and cry.” Related Stories Taylor Swift to Perform at Academy Museum Gala Taylor Swift Fires Up Academy Gala With Four Songs in Her First Band Performance Since the Eras Tour The festival presented Kore-eda with its Cinema Honorary Award at the National Museum of Singapore before an onstage conversation with festival chair Boo Junfeng, the filmmaker behind “Apprentice.” Introduced in 2014, the award is the festival’s top honor and recognizes lasting contributions to Asian cinema. Previous recipients include Im Kwon-taek, Garin Nugroho, Jafar Panahi and Deepa Mehta. Popular on Variety Kore-eda said his methods with children have grown more flexible. Through “Shoplifters” and the films he made abroad, “The Truth” and “Broker,” he did not hand children scripts. Instead, he rewrote dialogue around the personality and vocabulary of the children he met at auditions, so that they only spoke lines they could say with conviction, and then fed them lines on set or described a situation and let them talk freely. On “Monster,” he gave the young cast scripts, judging that the subject was risky enough that separating the children from their roles was safer. He now decides child by child and film by film, he said. Two directors shaped that approach. Hou Hsiao-hsien , Kore-eda said, joins in when children are playing in a scene, slips out once the camera is rolling and lets them keep going – a trick Kore-eda now uses himself. Atchity died Monday of kidney failure at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, his longtime business and producing partner, Chi-Li Wong, told The Hollywood Reporter . Atchity also was behind 16 romantic telefilms made under the banner of Shades of Love that were produced for cable and video. They ran in Canada and on HBO/Cinemax in the States and were released internationally by Warner Bros. Other producing credits included the 1989 telefilm The Amityville Horror: The Evil Escapes and the 2010 documentary The Kennedy Detail . An author of more than 20 books, Atchity headed Story Merchant Books, selling his clients’ work to publishers and to film and television outlets while publishing many other works himself. articles.summary: Writer-director Stelana Kliris’ feature, starring Leem Lubany and Luca Pasqualino and inspired by the experiences of her refugee parents, will open PÖFF’s Critics’ Picks section.
articles.content: Can a young woman forced to leave a divided Cyprus in the 1970s find belonging and even love in an arranged marriage in Apartheid South Africa, especially when a secret from her past threatens to change everything? With Apart , South African Cypriot writer-director Stelana Kliris ( Find Me Falling , Committed ) has created a deeply personal film about displacement, belonging, borders, both the ones that are physical and those that are in our hearts, and human connections. And it is inspired by the real experiences of her refugee parents. The movie, world-premiering at the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF), stars Leem Lubany ( Omar , Rock the Kasbah ), Luca Pasqualino ( Rivals , The Musketeers ) and Girley Jazama ( Under the Hanging Tree , The White Line ). The 1 vs. 1 fighting game took place in feudal Japan and launched in arcades in 1993. The figures from the filing might not demonstrate the full costs associated with production, given that the company — which exists to assist with filming reimbursements in the U.K. — has been associated with previous productions, including “The Nevers,” when it took on the name Roundabout Productions. HBO declined comment. But, despite the elevated numbers — the first movie worked on a $125 million budget — an individual familiar with the matter told TheWrap that episodic budgets are on par with HBO’s world-building shows like “Game of Thrones” spinoff “House of the Dragon” and “The Last of Us.” The final season of “GOT” reportedly cost about $15 million per episode, while “House of the Dragon” has been valued at $15-$20 million and “Last of Us” at $10-$15 million. The elevated costs also account for an up front investment for HBO to create sets and infrastructure that will be used across the seven seasons, though only two seasons have been officially greenlit, with production on Season 2 kicking off this fall. That infrastructure even includes a school building for children actors to attend for the next decade.

articles.title: ‘Color Book’ Director David Fortune Used Ice Cold Showers to Practice His AT&T Untold Stories Award Pitch — Watch
articles.summary: The 2023 AT&T award winner stopped by IndieWire's Future of Filmmaking Summit to explain his preparation for the biggest pitch of his life.
articles.content: The AT&T Untold Stories Award is the world’s largest filmmaking award of its kind. Each year, hundreds of filmmakers apply to be considered for a prize that includes $1.2 million and a network of mentorship and support to help them make a film . Those candidates are narrowed down to five finalists who get a chance to pitch their film in front of a packed audience and a panel of judges at the Tribeca Festival. Win them over, and you might get a chance to bring your cinematic vision to life. David Fortune knows just how impactful the prize can be. The filmmaker, who won the 2023 AT&T Untold Stories Award, used the grant to make his 2024 feature “Color Book,” which is now streaming on Netflix. It tells a nuanced story about Black single parenthood that we had seldom seen on screen, all filtered through the voice of one distinctly talented filmmaker. During a conversation at IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking Summit, presented by AT&T, Fortune explained how he approached an opportunity that turned out to be life-changing. “I would say preparation,” Fortune said when asked to give advice to future contestants. “You can’t control if you win or lose, but you can control how you prepare. articles.content: You’ll never look at a wicker basket the same way after “Wicker”. Based on Ursula Wills-Jones’s short story “The Wicker Husband”, the raunchy period comedy follows an outcast Fisherwoman ( Olivia Colman ) commissioning a master Basket Weaver (Peter Dinklage) to make her a wicker husband. The result is a man entirely woven of wicker whose dedication to his wife and romance is absolute; of course, it’s a role for Alexander Skarsgård . Transforming the 6’4″ Swede into the Wicker Husband required not actual magic, but something very close to it. Art director and prosthetic makeup designer Joe Dunckley, as well as makeup and hair designer Sarah Rubano from Wētā Workshop, and their teams collaborated with directors Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer on creating a fully practical suit and full facial prosthetic makeup so that Skarsgård could move and emote as freely as the romance novel-inspired poster for “Wicker” promises. Eleanor had done this before, most notably for her groundbreaking 1991 documentary “Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker’s Apocalypse,” which served as an all-access pass to her husband, Francis Ford Coppola , laying it all on the line to produce “Apocalypse Now.” But unlike that project, Eleanor’s “ Marie Antoinette ” footage has gone untouched. articles.summary: A reimagining of the Baba Yaga myth (and her own play), Kat Sandler's AMC+ series follows a beat cop and a private investigator as they search a misty, mysterious coastal town for a powerful family's missing heir.
articles.content: When the name Baba Yaga is first thrown out in Kat Sandler’s series, “Yaga,” the reaction is what you’d expect from any thirty-something guy in the year 2026: “Wait, the one from ‘John Wick’ ?” The response doubles as an acknowledgement of and explanation for a title that, on its own, sounds weirdly incomplete: “Oh, OK: They couldn’t call it ‘Baba Yaga’ because then everyone would think it’s a ‘John Wick’ show. So it’s just called, ‘Yaga.’ Because it’s actually about witches.” But “Yaga” is also weirdly incomplete in execution, mainly because it’s not nearly weird enough. Adapted from Sandler’s play of the same name, the eight-episode series reimagines the Baba Yaga myth as a detective-driven mystery — not the myth about Keanu Reeves’ unkillable assassin, but the historical one from Slavic folklore about a witch who, depending on the teller, is either a nice, accommodating, elderly woman, or a kidnapping, kid-eating monster. articles.content: Black Bear CEO Teddy Schwarzman has seen some ups and downs in the transition from financier-producer-foreign-sales-company-UK-distributor to full-on North American distribution company Black Bear Pictures. The Blackstone scion is smart and experienced enough to know the risks inherent in competing in the fraught indie marketplace. But even in the face of frosty reviews for “Christy,” starring Sydney Sweeney with her bosom buried from view in a boxing movie, he mounted a full-on theatrical release and demonstrated his support for the filmmakers and would-be Oscar contender. That didn’t happen. The $15-million movie grossed just under $2 million domestic. articles.content: “ Project Hail Mary ” was “the hardest movie” that Phil Lord and Chris Miller ever made — and they’re able to show their work. The filmmaking duo behind one of the year’s biggest hits built a deck to lead an audience through the challenging (but positive!) production process in a keynote presentation at IndieWire ‘s Future of Filmmaking 2026 Summit presented by AT&T. articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on January 28, 2026 at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. Sony Pictures Classics will release the film in theaters on Friday, October 23.] It’s become commonplace in recent years: movies set in New York , telling distinctly New York stories, yet shot entirely somewhere else like Ireland. Given Hollywood’s economic slowdown, an indie production can be forgiven for doing whatever it takes to get a film made. Still, many films no longer seem interested in even attempting to suspend disbelief about place. Which makes ” The Only Living Pickpocket in New York ” feel like a minor miracle and a welcome update to the New York crime movie genre. Writer/director Noah Segan shoots not only in Manhattan, but across the city’s outer boroughs like the Bronx, Queens, and Brooklyn, capturing a New York that feels authentic rather than postcard-ready. The film’s most satisfying image arrives late: a 360 view of the harbor skyline seen not from lower Manhattan but from the murky New Jersey shoreline, lensed by Sam Levy with bracing clarity. Though the credits list a Los Angeles unit, its scenes disappear seamlessly into the world of the film. articles.summary: Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer's second feature is a kooky sex-crazed folk tale in search of a greater purpose beyond its premise, but Colman and Skarsgård prove irresistibly weird and wonderful.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on January 25, 2026 at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. Black Bear will release the film in limited theaters on Friday, October 23 with expansion to follow on Friday, October 30.] A kooky sex-crazed folk tale in search of a larger purpose beyond its whimsical premise, Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer’s “Wicker” stars Olivia Colman as a prickly fisherwoman who emerges from the fringes of a seaside village to task a basketmaker (Peter Dinklage) with weaving her a husband. That husband is played by a delightfully deadpan Alexander Skarsgård as a man made entirely of wicker fibers, a face that looks like a woven espadrille stretched over a human skull. Sure, the premise — originating from a story called “The Wicker Husband” by Ursula Wills-Jones — is a novel one destined to grab attention.
